scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A wall bounces light too, so why can you see yourself in a mirror, but not in a white wall?

scenes.name: glass
scenes.text: A mirror is glass with a thin coat of metal behind it, usually silver or aluminium, then protective paint.

scenes.name: electrons
scenes.text: Metals have free electrons that respond to light, and send almost all of it straight back.

scenes.name: smooth
scenes.text: The surface is extremely smooth, so every ray bounces at the same angle it came in.

scenes.name: wall
scenes.text: A wall is rough at a tiny scale. Light scatters in all directions, so you see brightness, not an image.

scenes.name: flip
scenes.text: Mirrors don't really swap left and right. They reverse front and back, which looks like a left-right swap.

scenes.name: uses
scenes.text: Curved mirrors focus light, in car side mirrors, telescopes and solar power plants.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Smooth metal, straight bounce, a clear image. Follow for more on how things really work.
